items.title: Remote UX Work: Guidelines and Resources
items.summary: Even though in-person UX sessions are typically ideal, sometimes budget or travel restrictions necessitate remote UX work. This article presents guidelines for remote user research, UX workshops or presentations, and collaboration.

items.title: Persuasive Storytelling Rule #1: Adapt Your Vocabulary
items.summary: Storytelling is a powerful technique for UX teams and for working with stakeholders, but only if you use the proper words for your audience's domain. Here are tips for building vocabulary for your stories.

items.title: Service Blueprinting: Fails and Fixes
items.summary: The most common pain points with service blueprinting are setting expectations, determining scope, and communicating insights, according to 97 UX professionals.

items.title: Discovery: Definition
items.summary: Although many different instigators, roles, and activities are involved in a discovery, all discoveries strive to achieve consensus on a problem to be solved and its desired outcomes.

items.title: Tools for Remote UX Workshops
items.summary: The type of workshop will dictate which tools your team should use. Ultimately, with limited time and budget, your best bet is to use a tool your team already knows how to use.

items.title: Foundational UX Workshop Activities
items.summary: There are 7 activities that act as a foundation for every UX exercise during a workshop or collaborative team meeting. By understanding these, you can create almost any other exercise you need.

items.title: Dualities of User Experience (Jakob Nielsen keynote)
items.summary: Many issues in the user-experience field don’t have a simple answer. Rather there’s a tension between two good answers that are often polar opposites. Both extremes can be useful perspectives, and both have their advocates when people debate UX. How do we resolve these differences? This was Jakob Nielsen's keynote at the UX Conference in Las Vegas.

items.title: UX Workshops vs. Meetings: What's the Difference?
items.summary: Meetings are for sharing information; workshops are for solving a problem or reaching an actionable goal. We compare the differences in purpose, scope, length, structure, and preparation time for workshops and meetings.

items.title: Top Tasks for UX Design: How and Why to Create Them
items.summary: Top Tasks are a tool used to focus a design team on the same, best set of user tasks. It comprises a list of 10 or fewer activities that users should be able to achieve using a design. If people can’t do these things, the design has failed. It takes a small amount of effort to create Top Tasks lists, but their impact is great.

items.title: Six Pillars Supporting Better and Easier UX
items.summary: Great design doesn't just happen. Rather, the organization must build 6 pillars that carry UX to success: capabilities, executive support, teams, resources, process, and schedule.

items.title: 10 Best Intranets of 2020: What Makes Them Great
items.summary: Clear vision, Agile development, and the goal to connect coworkers are what distinguishes the best intranets.

items.title: How to Get Stakeholders to Sketch: A Magic Formula
items.summary: Collaborative sketching is a powerful tool for building buy-in for design decisions; however, it can be difficult to get stakeholders comfortable with the idea of drawing in a group setting. These variables help make group sketching more productive and effective with stakeholders.

items.title: 5 UX Workshops and When to Use Them: A Cheat Sheet
items.summary: 5 common UX workshops, explained. Learn about 5 UX workshops and how to use them within the design process.

items.title: User Need Statements in Design Thinking
items.summary: Before you draw a single pixel, define what user need you're trying to solve with the (next-step) user-experience design. UX should be grounded in real user needs.

items.title: Service Blueprinting: Top Questions Answered
items.summary: Service blueprints are the primary tool for service design, but practitioners often misunderstand how they relate to journey mapping, who should be involved in the process, and how to sell their value to the organization.

items.title: How to Get Stakeholders to Sketch: A Magic Formula
items.summary: In ideation and many other UX activities, we want to include stakeholders and get them to participate in sketching UI prototypes and other visuals. Here are four tactics to getting everybody to sketch in your UX workshops.

items.title: Facilitating UX Workshops with Stakeholders in the Room
items.summary: How to maximize the positive contribution of a variety of stakeholders in workshops throughout the UX design process while minimizing any disruptive or negative impact.

items.title: The "Parking Lot" in UX Workshops: Friend or Foe?
items.summary: To maintain focus in a UX workshop, set aside ideas in a "parking lot" if they diverge from the stated agenda. Parked ideas should be discussed later when they won't slow the team's momentum in addressing the meeting's main topic. Here are 3 guidelines for making the most of a parking lot.

items.title: DesignOps FAQ: 6 Common Questions About Design Operations
items.summary: Because the field is being defined in real time, practitioners often have questions about what Design Operations means, and how to establish DesignOps practices.

items.title: Design Thinking Is Like Cooking
items.summary: As you learn design thinking, you progress through stages: being a beginner, an intermediate practitioner, and possessing advanced expertise. This progression is like learning to cook: you won't be a master chef on day 1, but there are appropriate skills to aim for at each level.
